key_insight: KaiNinja extends a native single-image 3D generator from fused whole-object meshes to part-level 3D assets by replacing the original O-Voxel setup with a dual-volume representation that can model touching part interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, mask-free generation of editable, riggable, and simulation-ready part-based 3D models without adding a separate segmentation stage.
method: Built on TRELLIS.2 and reformulated its O-Voxel representation into dual volumes.
Avoids post-hoc 3D segmentation by generating part structure directly during synthesis.
Trained on mixed part-level data, including CAD models and agent-authored assets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 40% lower whole-object Chamfer distance and a 16% higher strict part F-score versus part-generation pipelines across different paradigms, while also noting improved whole-object fidelity over the same backbone fine-tuned on the same data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and diversity of part-level training data, and the dual-volume design may add implementation complexity compared with a standard single-volume generator.
paper_title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level
